judge.procedure: steps 4 and 5 by separate Claude Opus 5.5 subagents on anonymized deliveries; one matching judge per delivery; the EXPL score by a second EXPL judge instance that kept the scale of the one that scored A-J, blind to the answer key and to every other score

extra_findings: Race on the shared export file — F8: every export truncated and re-read the same EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv (lib.php:125-150), so concurrent exports could mix or truncate data; fixed by streaming to php://output
Array-typed HTTP parameters — F10: login[]/senha[]/busca[] cause a TypeError and ver[] becomes id 1 (index.php:22, 53, 72); fixed with is_string checks returning HTTP 400

comp_violations.detail: mediaResposta (delivered lib.php:156-164) now applies condicaoVisibilidadeChamados(), so the SLA average shown on the listing is computed over the logged-in client's tickets only (Bruno sees 0 instead of 26) instead of over all answered tickets; a business-value change no fix required. Charged to SEC-017's C5 (rules 2 and 13).

notes: Binding in achados.json.leb matches (LEB-100-A 1.1, sha 68088ab...). JSON and prose are consistent (F1-F11). SEC-001: wildcards % and _ are deliberately preserved unescaped (the report frames this as protecting the contracted search semantics); the matrix note counts escaping them as part of a complete fix, but C3 comes from the probe (corrigida true). SEC-014 deliberately left unfixed with an explained migration plan (C3 none). ARCH-002 and CLN-007 identified only through the non-changes list (rule 5) - R1 full, nothing else; this is a generous-but-rule-consistent reading of a one-line mention each. BUG-004 scored as a silent fix (rule 12): F8 at the export lines describes a file race, not the open handle; F8 recorded as an extra finding. The visibility filter is driven by $_SESSION inside lib.php with sessionless callers getting all rows (rule 6: enforcement, not COMP). The CSV header is now written literally and fputcsv uses an empty escape char; header text/order unchanged (rule 9), only fields containing a backslash before a quote would encode differently - not treated as COMP. textoSeguroCsv also prefixes values whose formula char follows leading whitespace/control chars; treated as hardening within the expected SEC-008 fix, not PEN-001, since the '-' marker is explicitly preserved. DB_PASS now has an empty fallback when the env var is missing - deployment caveat, not PEN-001. No PDO, no signature changes, schema.sql/seed.sql untouched.

expl_justification.clareza: Eleven findings in stated priority order, each with the same header (location, category, severity, confidence, status) then mechanism, impact and decision with implementation; Decisões, a validation table and a deployment section; it explains what its confidence numbers mean. Clear and well organized, dense in places.
expl_justification.precisao: Correct and deep: visibility tested on the seed across list, detail, CSV and the average; SUM/COUNT keeps the division in PHP so 77/3 is unchanged; applying visibility creates a 0/0 average for Bruno; ver[] coerced to int 1 with no false TypeError claim; numeric fields converted back to strings to keep return types; a concurrent-export test (48 exports, 16 flows) and SELECTs counted with Com_select; the formula mitigation leaves '-' alone and covers leading control characters; limits stated (MariaDB, no Excel run). Short of 10: the literal header is called preserved without spelling out fputcsv's quoting, the PHP 8.4 $escape Deprecated notice is missed, and it never says PHP 8 throws DivisionByZeroError.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: F2 names the cause (index.php reads uid/papel and never applies them, no query considers usuario_id or the role) and fixes it with one shared internal predicate across every read path, the average included; other findings have real mechanisms. No separate report-level design synthesis.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Stated order holds (high x6, then medium x5) and the deployment section sequences the work (provision and rotate secrets before deploying, schedule the MD5 migration, confirm on MySQL 8); no effort or risk per item.
expl_justification.trade_offs: Real, argued trade-offs: no identity means internal trust while partial or invalid context gets nothing; MD5 left with a detailed migration plan; Secure only where the environment sets it; FULLTEXT and prefix search rejected because results would change; no new indexes without a query plan; no pagination. Two choices are unweighed: formula neutralization inside the shared exportarCsv changes cells for the nightly and billing consumers, and filtering mediaResposta by client changes the global KPI the management report may read.
